solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jumps on bed — child's play

parts.note: jumps on one leg are hops
a cot is a small bed for a baby
CH is a standard abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child bouncing on the bed, which grown-ups dismiss as mere child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's play' reads as one idiom, but 'child's' gives CH and only 'play' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game, so it is a kind of play.

clue.text: Obstruct crime

definitions.meaning: a robbery at gunpoint is called a ...

explanation.surface: A brief accusation: someone blocking justice and committing an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to delay or block, and the noun names an armed robbery.

clue.text: Risk as queen enters large building briefly

indicators.note: the queen goes into the shortened building, so one piece enters the other
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A security worry as the monarch walks into a grand building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of the building, and 'enters' signals the royal abbreviation going inside; a pile is the stately-home sense of building.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is danger, a direct synonym of risk.

clue.text: Force prisoners to study

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts
to train is to study for a skill

explanation.surface: Making inmates attend lessons against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel them, the verb sense of force.

clue.text: Radio quiz score — son's quite excited

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: being excited, the letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: son's is read as son is, giving the letters SONS

explanation.surface: A boy thrilled at the score on a radio quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges SONS plus QUITE to give QUESTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty Questions was a long-running BBC radio panel game of guessing objects.

clue.text: Gardens surrounding minute houses

indicators.note: the gardening verb goes around the small piece, so it surrounds it

parts.note: to garden can be to hoe, so gardens is hoes

explanation.surface: Planted beds wrapping round tiny cottages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gardens' and 'houses' are both verbs here, though they read as nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: To house someone is to give them a place to live, as homes does as a verb.

clue.text: Father needs two secretaries

indicators.note: two asks for the same short piece to appear twice in a row

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A busy dad who requires a pair of assistants.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an affectionate word for a dad.

clue.text: Display herb with lid removed in food cupboard

indicators.note: in says the trimmed herb sits inside the cupboard word

parts.note: a pantry is a cupboard or small room for food

indicators.note: in a down clue the lid is the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: Showing off a herb jar, opened, in the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with lid removed' drops the S of SAGE to leave AGE, which goes into PANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is splendid ceremonial show, a sense of display.

clue.text: French city with very good banks receiving zero investment?

indicators.note: the pious word takes in the round letter, so it receives it

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crosswordese for very good
an investment of zero is nothing, the letter O
tiers are rows or banks, as of seats

explanation.surface: A French city whose virtuous banks have attracted no investment at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests money but means rows, TIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Poitiers is a historic city in west-central France.

clue.text: Criminal protects my girl

indicators.note: the criminal wraps round the exclamation, protecting it

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who deals in stolen goods
Lor! is an old exclamation like My!

explanation.surface: A crook guarding the speaker's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, LOR, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is a girl's name.

clue.text: Maybe weekly food for bird

parts.note: a weekly publication may be a magazine, a mag
a pie is a dish of food

explanation.surface: A weekly publication's treat being fed to a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white crow-family bird.

clue.text: On Scottish island regularly eats fish

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word eats

explanation.surface: On a Hebridean island someone routinely dines on fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The mullet is a common sea fish.

clue.text: Island one hidden by tip of distant continent

indicators.note: the tip here is the end letter of distant
the continent conceals the person, so it is placed inside

parts.note: Asia is a continent
one, as in a person, is a man

explanation.surface: An island where a person hides at the far end of a remote continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of distant' is its last letter, T, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the large island state south of mainland Australia.

clue.text: Base school leader's without mercy

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the head's word goes around

parts.note: a school's leader is the head; with the 's it gives HEADS
to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy

explanation.surface: A merciless headteacher described as rather base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it has its older sense of outside, so the possessive wraps round the word for mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is an organisation's base of operations.

clue.text: Setter talked of career with small remuneration? That's about right

indicators.note: talked of says a word is spoken, so we want something sounding like it

parts.note: to career is to rush along, as to hare does

indicators.note: the pay word goes about the letter for right

parts.note: remuneration is pay

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler grumbling about poor pay for the job, asking if that is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the definition: a product that sets hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairspray is applied to fix a hairstyle in place, so it is a setter.

clue.text: Heavyweight captured by Scottish hero heading off suddenly

indicators.note: the weight goes inside the hero, captured by him
the first letter of the hero's name is cut off

parts.note: William Wallace led Scottish resistance to England in the 1290s
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight fighter seized by a Scottish hero who abruptly leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' loses the hero's first letter, giving ALLACE, and 'captured by' places the weight inside; William Wallace is the Braveheart of Scottish history.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means abruptly, without warning, as suddenly does.

clue.text: Actress nervously accepting lead in comedy? Most unusual

indicators.note: the scrambled actress takes in the extra letter, accepting it
nervously suggests the letters are jittery and rearranged
lead in takes the first letter of comedy

explanation.surface: A jittery actress taking on a leading comic role, which is most unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' rearranges ACTRESS into SCAREST, and 'accepting' adds C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcest is the superlative of scarce, rarest, which matches most unusual.

clue.text: Review of part of match edited in a later copy

indicators.note: edited suggests text reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports broadcast replaying a passage of play in a later recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges IN A LATER COPY.
explanation.definitionFit: An action replay shows a moment of sport again, a review of part of a match.

clue.text: Boy has written up ten lines of poetry

parts.note: a boy is a son

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A boy has composed ten lines of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns TEN into NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem.

clue.text: Chance of harlot getting kissed when picked up?

indicators.note: picked up is heard, so the phrase is spoken and matched by ear

parts.note: a harlot is a pro, and getting kissed is pecked: the pro's pecked

explanation.surface: A prostitute's odds of a kiss, said with a wink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests the harlot's trade but means heard: PRO'S PECKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a likelihood or chance of something happening.

clue.text: Place in Surrey for one actor

parts.note: for one means for example, EG
a ham is an overacting actor

explanation.surface: A Surrey location suited to a single performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county south-west of London; Egham is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in Surrey, near Runnymede.

clue.text: Name of driving aid used in car test twice, when reversing

indicators.note: reversing turns the doubled letters so they read backwards
twice asks for the test's letters to appear two times

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK cars

explanation.surface: A satnav brand used during a driving test that involves reversing twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly vehicle safety check; doubled and turned it gives TOMTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: TomTom is a brand of satnav device that guides drivers.

clue.text: Dance: mother accompanies old boy doing the twist

parts.note: mam is a regional word for mother

indicators.note: twisting round makes the two letters face the other way

explanation.surface: Mum dances with an elderly gent doing the Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the twist' sounds like another dance but turns OB into BO.
explanation.definitionFit: The mambo is a Latin American dance from Cuba.

clue.text: Examine A-level result primarily during school inspection

indicators.note: the initials come during the school word, placed inside it
primarily takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Checking exam grades while inspectors visit a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Examine' looks like the definition but supplies its initial E; 'inspection' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A search is a careful examination, which is an inspection.

clue.text: Possibly mention time is a healer

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying that time is a healer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the first word, giving OINTMEN, and the abbreviation for time completes it; the surface plays on the proverb that time heals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is a salve that heals sores, a healer.

clue.text: Remain in dinghy at sea, drifting back

indicators.note: drifting back means the found letters run backwards
in says the letters sit within the words dinghy at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor staying in a small boat as it floats backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'dinghY AT Sea' is YATS, which 'drifting back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain in place.

clue.text: Excluded young female solicitor, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the phrase is heard, matched by sound

parts.note: a young female is a miss, and a solicitor is a tout touting for trade

explanation.surface: A young woman lawyer left out, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer but means someone soliciting custom, a TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be missed out is to be left out, excluded.
